fields.label: Core problem
fields.value: Package applications into isolated, portable environments while sharing operating-system resources and coordinating those environments at cluster scale.

fields.label: Mechanism chain
fields.value: Application dependencies/configuration -> container artifact/runtime -> isolated process environment -> shared kernel -> orchestration -> cluster management -> scaling/observability.

fields.label: Central insight
fields.value: Containerization is not merely packaging software. In the supplied source it is a layered system spanning virtualization boundaries, application packaging, standardized images/runtimes/distribution, orchestration and cluster operations, with a distinct shared-kernel security model.

fields.label: Core problem
fields.value: Package and execute applications consistently across differing computing environments while isolating processes, controlling resources, distributing images, coordinating multi-container applications, and supporting clustered container services.

fields.label: Central model
fields.value: Application + dependencies -> Dockerfile/build -> read-only image -> registry distribution -> container runtime -> isolated processes + shared kernel -> Compose/Swarm coordination -> persistent volumes where required.

fields.label: Central insight
fields.value: Docker is best understood as a connected packaging, runtime, distribution and orchestration ecosystem: images define reusable software artifacts, containers instantiate them, the Linux kernel supplies isolation/resource primitives, registries distribute artifacts, Compose coordinates applications, and Swarm clusters Docker Engines.
